judgment.explanation: 蘇峻 is the subject of the story, a rebel general who arrived at Stone City (石頭). The candidate 蘇峻 matches the canonical name and the historical context of the 蘇峻 rebellion during the Eastern Jin. The Liu annotation also refers to 峻 as 蘇峻, confirming identity.

The surface 王 appears in the Liu annotation in the phrase 討王, which is ambiguous. The candidate is 王恭, but the text 討王 in the annotation context (about 蘇峻's biography) does not clearly identify which 王 is being referred to. The supplied candidate 王恭 is not clearly supported by the evidence, and the referent of 王 here is uncertain.

峻 is the personal name of 蘇峻, used in the Liu annotation. The annotation text 徵峻峻/敦有功封公遷歷陽太守 clearly refers to 蘇峻, and the semantic record confirms coreference with the main-text mention of 蘇峻. The candidate 蘇峻 matches.

王隱 is the author of the 王隱晉書, cited in the Liu annotation. The candidate 王隱 matches the canonical name and the role as author of the cited historical work. The annotation text 王隱晉書曰 confirms this identity.

review.explanation: The mention surface is 蘇峻, the full canonical name. The main text explicitly states 蘇峻既至石頭, and the Liu annotation (annotation-003) repeatedly refers to 峻 in the context of the same rebel general. The candidate evidence from people.json provides the canonical name 蘇峻. The main text and annotation context unambiguously identify this as Su Jun, the rebel general. No contradicting evidence exists.

The surface 峻 is an abbreviated personal name. Annotation-003 states 詔書徵峻峻 and 峻外營將表白鼓自鳴峻, clearly referring to the same 蘇峻 from the main text. The coreference chain links this mention to sfh1-mention-14781a7673e50f18f45c5aed (蘇峻) and sfh1-mention-cea76d9cf914ae6575ea132d (峻 with courtesy name 子高). The annotation context about the rebel general matches the main text's 蘇峻. No distinctness or contradicting evidence is present.

The surface 王隱 is the full name of the author of 王隱晉書, cited in annotation-001. The candidate evidence from people.json provides the canonical name 王隱. The reference semantics explicitly mark this as distinct from 蘇峻 mentions and from the 王 surname reference in annotation-002. The annotation text 王隱晉書曰 clearly identifies 王隱 as the author of the cited work. No contradicting evidence exists.

The surface 峻 is an abbreviated personal name for 蘇峻. Annotation-001 states 峻字子高, and the alias registry evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-754d73eeff01f27628e0) confirms 蘇峻's courtesy name is 子高, providing a direct biographical link. The coreference chain connects this mention to the main text's 蘇峻 (sfh1-mention-14781a7673e50f18f45c5aed). The reference semantics explicitly distinguish this from 王隱 and the 王 surname reference. The alias evidence directly supports the identity resolution.

The mention '子高' is explicitly identified as the courtesy name (字) of 蘇峻 in the Liu Xiaobiao annotation (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-034-liu-annotation-001), which states '峻字子高'. The candidate evidence from aliases.json (sfh1-candidate-evidence-4f1dcb42b99997c1c3ca) independently confirms this: '蘇峻字子高'. The main text (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-034-main) discusses 蘇峻's rebellion at 石頭, and the annotation chain (sfh1-ev-05-fangzheng-034-liu-annotation-001 through -005) provides biographical details consistent with 蘇峻's known career (舉孝廉, 討王敦, 歷陽太守, rebellion). The reference semantics correctly identify '子高' as a courtesy name, not a kinship term. The suffix '子' is part of the courtesy name itself. No contradicting evidence exists. The identity resolution is well-supported by direct textual evidence.

assertions.interpretation: The scene is set at the time when Su Jun had already arrived at Stone City (Shitou), marking the onset of the crisis.
At this same moment, the assembled officials scattered and fled, contemporaneous with Su Jun's arrival.
At the same scene time, only Palace Attendant Zhong Ya alone remained at the emperor's side.

assertions.exact_span: 君性亮直必不容於寇讎
assertions.interpretation: A prediction about Zhong Ya's future: given his upright nature, he will inevitably not be tolerated by the enemy.
assertions.surface: 君性亮直必不容於寇讎

assertions.exact_span: 何不用隨時之宜而坐待其弊邪
assertions.interpretation: An exhortation to act according to the circumstances rather than sit and await ruin, referring to the present moment of crisis.
assertions.surface: 何不用隨時之宜而坐待其弊邪

assertions.exact_span: 值中原亂招合流舊三千餘家結壘本縣
assertions.interpretation: Background: when the Central Plains fell into chaos, Su Jun gathered over three thousand displaced households and built fortifications in his home county.
assertions.surface: 值中原亂招合流舊三千餘家結壘本縣

assertions.interpretation: After a while, an imperial edict summoned Su Jun, a background event preceding the main scene.
Background: Su Jun was enfeoffed as a duke and promoted to Grand Administrator of Liyang, prior to the rebellion.
The imperial forces were defeated, a later outcome following the events of the main scene.

assertion.exact_span: 見可而進知難而退古之道也
assertion.interpretation: A quoted ancient principle invoked by the speaker urging Zhong Ya to advance when possible and retreat when facing difficulty.
assertion.surface: 見可而進知難而退古之道也

assertion.exact_span: 吾懼董狐將執簡而進矣
assertion.interpretation: Zhong Ya invokes the historical precedent of Dong Hu, the upright historian, as a future threat that the record will be written against those who flee.
assertion.surface: 吾懼董狐將執簡而進矣

assertion.interpretation: Background on Su Jun: in his youth he had talent and learning and served as registrar of the commandery.

assertion.exact_span: 峻率衆二萬濟自横江至於蔣山
assertion.interpretation: Background: Su Jun led 20,000 troops crossing from Hengjiang and reaching Jiangshan, the military advance leading up to the scene at Stone City.
assertion.surface: 峻率衆二萬濟自横江至於蔣山

assertion.exact_span: 我寧山頭望廷尉不能廷尉望山頭乃作亂
assertion.interpretation: A quoted statement attributed to Su Jun expressing his resolve: he would rather look down at the court from the mountain than have the court look at him from the mountain, and thus he rebelled.
assertion.surface: 我寧山頭望廷尉不能廷尉望山頭乃作亂
